name: ICCTG PPS–hydroxyzine
aliases: Interstitial Cystitis Clinical Trials Group pilot trial
question: Do oral pentosan polysulfate sodium, hydroxyzine, or their combination improve patient-reported global response in interstitial cystitis?

arms.label: Oral pentosan polysulfate sodium plus hydroxyzine

design.population: 121 randomized adults had cystoscopy- and hydrodistention-confirmed NIH–NIDDK interstitial cystitis, at least 11 voids daily, and pain/discomfort of at least 4/9 for at least 24 weeks.
design.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, pp 810–811; Table 2, p 811

verdictNote: Neither 24-week factorial comparison reached the prespecified two-sided 0.05 significance level.
takeaway: In the 24-week double-masked factorial pilot (n=121), global response occurred in 20/59 (34%) with PPS versus 11/62 (18%) without PPS (P=0.064), and 19/61 (31%) with hydroxyzine versus 12/60 (20%) without hydroxyzine (P=0.26); neither main effect met the 0.05 threshold.

reports.label: Pilot factorial trial
reports.dateLocator: PubMed citation and Crossref published-print: September 2003; Europe PMC firstPublicationDate: 2003-09-01
reports.citation: Sant GR, Propert KJ, Hanno PM, et al. "A Pilot Clinical Trial of Oral Pentosan Polysulfate and Oral Hydroxyzine in Patients With Interstitial Cystitis." *J Urol.* 2003;170(3):810-815. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000083020.06212.3d
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, End points and Results, p 811; Table 3, p 812

results.measure: 24-week global response, intent-to-treat pooled PPS versus no PPS
results.note: 20/59 (34%) with PPS versus 11/62 (18%) without PPS; withdrawals before 24 weeks counted as nonresponders.
results.locator: Full text, End points and Results, p 811; Table 3, p 812

results.measure: 24-week global response, intent-to-treat pooled hydroxyzine versus no hydroxyzine
results.note: 19/61 (31%) with hydroxyzine versus 12/60 (20%) without hydroxyzine; withdrawals before 24 weeks counted as nonresponders.
results.locator: Full text, End points and Results, p 811; Table 3, p 812

results.endpoint: Symptom indexes, pain, urgency, and frequency
results.measure: 24-week changes among participants with complete secondary data
results.note: No statistically significant differences in pain, urgency, frequency, IC symptom/problem indexes, or Wisconsin IC score; 96/121 had complete secondary data, so these analyses were not intent-to-treat.
results.locator: Full text, Results, pp 811–812; Tables 3–4, p 812

results.endpoint: Patient-reported global response by individual randomized arm
results.measure: 24-week response in each arm, with early withdrawals counted as nonresponders
results.locator: Full text, Results, p 811; Table 4, p 812

harms.label: Adverse events
harms.note: At least one event: hydroxyzine 50/61 (82%) versus no hydroxyzine 51/60 (85%); PPS 50/59 (85%) versus no PPS 51/62 (82%). Worst Common Toxicity Criteria grade 3: 9/61 versus 13/60 and 12/59 versus 10/62, respectively.
harms.locator: Full text, Results and Table 5, pp 812–813

harms.label: Serious adverse events
harms.value: Nine events; none considered related to study treatments.

delivery.label: Recruitment
delivery.value: 121 participants randomized over 18 months, 89% of a target of 136 planned for 10 months of recruitment.
delivery.locator: Full text, Statistics and Results, p 811

delivery.label: Complete follow-up
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, p 811; Table 3, p 812

delivery.label: Drug dosing
delivery.value: PPS 100 mg orally three times daily; hydroxyzine 10, then 25, then 50 mg orally at bedtime over three weeks, followed by the highest tolerated dose for 21 weeks.
delivery.locator: Full text, Interventions, pp 811–812; Table 1, p 811

delivery.label: Hydroxyzine target dose attained
delivery.value: 66% of hydroxyzine recipients reached 50 mg daily (71% hydroxyzine alone; 60% combination); 90% on equivalent placebo tolerated 50 mg (P=0.0019).
delivery.locator: Full text, Table 1, p 811; Results, p 812
